content:
Projectile motion describes the arc-shaped path of an object launched into the air, moving under the influence of gravity alone, while air resistance is often ignored.

The motion consists of two independent parts: horizontal and vertical. This type of motion creates a parabolic curve, similar to the flight of a ball or the launch of a cannonball.
A ball is launched with a speed of 20 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Find the maximum height reached.

Given:
		v = 20 m/s
		θ = 30°
		g = 9.8 m/s²
		H = ?

Where:
		H = Maximum Height (meters)
		v = Initial Velocity (m/s)
		θ = Launch Angle (degrees)
		g = Acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s²)
